title: Wilson et al. v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
summary: Members challenged a voting restriction imposed at a congregational meeting. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because BCO 43-1 permits complaints against acts or decisions of church courts, and a congregation is not such a court. It identified other possible routes through a report to Presbytery or review of church records. The adopted decision did not decide whether the voting restriction was constitutionally valid.

source_limits: Lengthy concurring, dissenting, and objecting opinions follow the adopted decision. Their substantive suffrage arguments are excluded from the synopsis.
evidence_notes: The complained-of action occurred in a congregational meeting rather than an act or decision of a church court.
The complaint was judicially out of order, unable to be put in order, and dismissed.
The adopted decision identified other procedural routes but did not adjudicate minor-communicant voting rights.
